verified.note: Solver adds unasked cause

harder.prompt_en: A school replaces its open courtyard with concrete, and its borewell level falls despite similar rainfall. Which would better help recharge groundwater: a recharge pit connected to roof drains or a larger concrete parking area? Why?
harder.prompt_hi: School apne khule courtyard par concrete bichha deta hai, aur lagbhag utni hi baarish ke bawajood borewell ka paani neeche chala jaata hai. Groundwater recharge ke liye roof drains se juda recharge pit behtar hai ya bada concrete parking area? Kyun?
harder.answer: A recharge pit connected to roof drains, because it lets rainwater seep into the ground.
acceptable: recharge pit because rainwater can soak into soil
recharge pit, kyunki baarish ka paani zameen mein ris sakta hai
hints: Which option gives rainwater a path below the surface?
Groundwater refills when rainwater can enter the ground.
Choose ___ because it lets rainwater ___.
The recharge pit: it lets roof rainwater seep underground.

verified.solverAnswer: Recharge pit connected to roof drains; it allows water to seep into ground instead of running off.
verified.note: Answers match key meaning

openers.prompt_en: A school science display needs a timekeeper that works indoors when sunlight is blocked and needs no battery. Choose: sundial or sand clock?
openers.prompt_hi: School science display ke liye aisa timekeeper chahiye jo dhoop na hone par bhi andar chale aur battery bhi na maange. Kya chunoge: sundial ya sand clock?
hints: Which option needs sunlight to work?
Think about what makes each clock show time.
Without sunlight, choose the ___.
Sand clock: falling sand works even without sunlight.

openers.prompt_en: During a lab activity, a pendulum takes 24 seconds to complete 12 oscillations. What is its time period?
openers.prompt_hi: Lab activity mein ek pendulum 12 oscillations poore karne mein 24 seconds leta hai. Uska time period kya hai?
hints: What does one time period measure?
Share the total time equally among all oscillations.
Time period = ___ ÷ number of oscillations.
2 seconds: divide 24 seconds by 12 oscillations.

harder.prompt_en: A museum must display a timekeeper that can mark passing time at night without electricity. Choose: sundial or water clock (ghati)? Give the reason in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Museum ko bina bijli ke raat mein beetta samay dikhane wala timekeeper rakhna hai. Kya chunoge: sundial ya water clock (ghati)? Ek chhote phrase mein wajah batao.
harder.answer: Water clock (ghati), because flowing water does not need sunlight
acceptable: water clock because it works at night
hints: Which option stops working when its shadow disappears?
Consider what each timekeeper needs to mark passing time.
Choose ___ because it does not depend on ___.
Water clock: flowing water can mark time without sunlight.

harder.prompt_en: Meera counts 15 oscillations of a pendulum in 27 seconds. For a school demonstration, how long should she expect 5 oscillations to take at the same rate?
harder.prompt_hi: Meera ek pendulum ke 15 oscillations 27 seconds mein ginti hai. Usi rate par school demonstration mein 5 oscillations ko kitna samay lagna chahiye?
harder.answer: 9 seconds
hints: How does the second count compare with the first?
At the same rate, time changes in the same proportion.
Expected time = 27 seconds × ___ ÷ 15.
9 seconds: five oscillations are one-third of fifteen.

harder.prompt_en: Two pendulums have equal thread lengths and small swings. Aditi doubles only the mass of one bob; Kabir shortens only the other thread. Whose pendulum has a shorter time period: Aditi's, Kabir's, or neither?
harder.prompt_hi: Do pendulums ki thread lengths barabar hain aur swings chhote hain. Aditi sirf ek bob ka mass double karti hai; Kabir sirf doosre ki thread chhoti karta hai. Kiska time period kam hoga: Aditi ka, Kabir ka, ya kisi ka nahi?
harder.answer: Kabir's
hints: Which change affects how quickly a pendulum swings?
Compare changing the thread with changing only the bob's mass.
The shorter time period belongs to ___ because its thread changed.
Kabir's: a shorter thread reduces the time period; extra bob mass does not.

openers.prompt_en: A skating app shows Meera’s speed as 2 m/s. What distance does this speed say she covers in one second?
openers.prompt_hi: Skating app Meera ki speed 2 m/s dikhata hai. Is speed ka matlab hai ki woh ek second mein kitni doori tay karti hai?
hints: What does a speed reading tell you about each second?
In m/s, the unit after the slash is the time unit.
In one second, she covers ___ metres.
She covers 2 metres in one second; that is what 2 m/s means.

openers.prompt_en: During a school sports event, a remote-controlled car travels 24 metres in 6 seconds. What is its average speed in m/s?
openers.prompt_hi: School sports event mein ek remote-controlled car 6 seconds mein 24 metres chalti hai. Uski average speed m/s mein kitni hai?
hints: How much distance does it cover in each second?
Divide the total distance by the total time.
Speed = 24 ÷ ___ m/s.
Its speed is 4 m/s because 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

harder.prompt_en: A metro travels at an average speed of 45 km/h. Its next stop is 15 km away. How many minutes will it take to reach the stop?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek metro ki average speed 45 km/h hai. Agla stop 15 km door hai. Wahan pahunchne mein kitne minutes lagenge?
harder.answer: 20 minutes
hints: First find the travel time in hours.
Time equals distance divided by speed; then convert hours to minutes.
Time in minutes = (15 ÷ ___) × 60.
It takes 20 minutes: 15 ÷ 45 hour equals one-third hour.

harder.prompt_en: In a cycling trial, Sana covers 900 m in 3 minutes. Dev covers 1,200 m in 5 minutes. Who is faster: Sana or Dev?
harder.prompt_hi: Cycling trial mein Sana 3 minutes mein 900 m chalti hai. Dev 5 minutes mein 1,200 m chalta hai. Kaun tez hai: Sana ya Dev?
harder.answer: Sana
hints: Can you compare their distances without considering time?
Find the distance each cyclist covers per minute.
First cyclist: 900 ÷ ___; second cyclist: 1,200 ÷ 5.
Sana is faster: 300 m/min exceeds Dev’s 240 m/min.

harder.prompt_en: A train’s speed display reads 72 km/h. Using 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s, what is that speed in m/s?
harder.prompt_hi: Train ki speed display par 72 km/h hai. Agar 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s, toh yeh speed m/s mein kitni hogi?
harder.answer: 20 m/s
hints: Which conversion factor is given?
Multiply the km/h reading by the stated factor.
Speed in m/s = 72 × ___ .
The speed is 20 m/s because 72 × 5/18 = 20.

openers.prompt_en: A robot moves along a straight school corridor. It travels 3 m in each 2-second interval. Is this uniform linear motion or non-uniform motion?
openers.prompt_hi: Ek robot school ke seedhe corridor mein chalta hai. Har 2 second mein woh 3 m chalta hai. Yeh uniform linear motion hai ya non-uniform motion?
hints: Is the path straight, and what happens in each interval?
Check both the direction of the path and distances over equal times.
Each 2-second interval has ___ m of travel.
Uniform linear motion: it covers equal distances in equal times along a straight path.

openers.prompt_en: A cyclist's distance from a starting point is 0 m, 4 m, 8 m and 12 m at 0, 2, 4 and 6 seconds. Is the motion uniform or non-uniform?
openers.prompt_hi: Ek cyclist ki starting point se doori 0, 2, 4 aur 6 second par 0 m, 4 m, 8 m aur 12 m hai. Motion uniform hai ya non-uniform?
hints: How much does the distance increase between readings?
Compare increases over time intervals of the same length.
The increases are ___, ___ and ___ metres.
Uniform: the distance increases by 4 m every 2 seconds.

harder.prompt_en: A skater covers 5 m in every second while circling a rink. Is this uniform linear motion? Answer yes or no, and give the key reason.
harder.prompt_hi: Ek skater rink ka chakkar lagate hue har second 5 m chalta hai. Kya yeh uniform linear motion hai? Haan ya nahin bolo, aur mukhya wajah batao.
harder.answer: No; the path is not straight.
hints: Does covering equal distances settle every part of the definition?
Think about the shape of the path, not just the timing.
The path is ___, so it fails the linear condition.
No: circling changes direction, so the motion is not along a straight line.

verified.solverAnswer: No. Circular path, not a straight line.
verified.note: Answers match key meaning

harder.prompt_en: A metro's position on a straight track is 0 m, 20 m, 50 m and 80 m at 0, 10, 20 and 30 seconds. Is its motion uniform or non-uniform over these intervals?
harder.prompt_hi: Seedhe track par metro ki position 0, 10, 20 aur 30 second par 0 m, 20 m, 50 m aur 80 m hai. In intervals mein motion uniform hai ya non-uniform?
harder.answer: Non-uniform
hints: Are positions the same as distances covered during each interval?
Subtract consecutive positions to find each interval's travel.
The interval distances are ___, ___ and ___ metres.
Non-uniform: the metro covers 20 m, then 30 m and 30 m in equal times.

harder.prompt_en: A delivery rider travels 6 km in the first 15 minutes and 2 km in the next 15 minutes. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek delivery rider pehle 15 minute mein 6 km aur agle 15 minute mein 2 km chalta hai. Poori trip ki average speed km/h mein kitni hai?
harder.answer: 16 km/h
hints: What are the total distance and total time?
Average speed uses the whole trip, not just one interval.
Average speed = ___ km ÷ ___ h.
16 km/h: the rider covers 8 km in half an hour.

openers.prompt_en: After a bite of idli leaves the stomach, which part of the digestive tract does it enter next: the small intestine or the large intestine?
openers.prompt_hi: Idli ka ek niwala stomach se nikalne ke baad digestive tract ke kis hisse mein jaata hai: small intestine ya large intestine?
hints: Which part comes immediately after the stomach?
Think of the route food follows, not the sizes of the parts.
Stomach → ___ → large intestine.
Small intestine; food enters it before the large intestine.

openers.prompt_en: At a school picnic, Meera eats a banana. In which part is most digested food absorbed into her body: the stomach or the small intestine?
openers.prompt_hi: School picnic mein Meera kela khaati hai. Digested food ka zyada hissa body mein kahaan absorb hota hai: stomach ya small intestine?
hints: Is churning the same as absorbing nutrients?
Look for the part where digested food passes into the body.
Most digested food is absorbed in the ___.
Small intestine; most digested food is absorbed there.

harder.prompt_en: A diagram labels the food pipe A, stomach B, small intestine C, large intestine D and rectum E. After food leaves B, which two labels does it pass through before reaching E?
harder.prompt_hi: Diagram mein food pipe A, stomach B, small intestine C, large intestine D aur rectum E hai. Food B se nikalne ke baad E tak pahunchne se pehle kaun se do labels se guzarta hai?
harder.answer: C, then D
hints: Trace the route forward from B.
Food reaches the intestines before the rectum.
C, then D; food passes through both intestines before the rectum.

harder.prompt_en: During diarrhoea, waste moves through the large intestine too quickly. Why might the body lose more water: less water is absorbed, or less food is chewed?
harder.prompt_hi: Diarrhoea mein waste large intestine se bahut jaldi guzarta hai. Body zyada paani kyun kho sakti hai: kam paani absorb hota hai, ya food kam chabaya jaata hai?
harder.answer: Less water is absorbed
acceptable: the large intestine absorbs less water
hints: What normally happens to water in the large intestine?
Think about what changes when waste spends less time there.
Less time in the large intestine means ___ water enters the body.
Less water is absorbed; waste passes through before much water can enter the body.

harder.prompt_en: A science poster swaps these labels: ‘bile from the pancreas’ and ‘digestive juice from the liver’. Which correction is right: bile comes from the liver, or bile comes from the stomach?
harder.prompt_hi: Science poster par labels ulte lage hain: ‘bile from the pancreas’ aur ‘digestive juice from the liver’. Sahi correction kya hai: bile liver se aata hai, ya stomach se?
harder.answer: Bile comes from the liver
hints: Which organ makes bile?
The pancreas makes a different digestive juice.
Bile comes from the ___.
Bile comes from the liver; the pancreas supplies its own digestive juice.

openers.prompt_en: A mosquito feeds on blood through a thin tube-like mouthpart. Does it take in food by biting and chewing, sucking, or swallowing whole?
openers.prompt_hi: Machhar apne patle, nali jaise mouthpart se khoon leta hai. Woh khaana kaise leta hai: kaatkar chabaata hai, choosta hai, ya poora nigalta hai?
hints: Can a thin tube break food into pieces?
Think about how liquid moves through a tube.
The mosquito takes in blood by ____.
Sucking: it draws liquid blood through its mouthpart.

openers.prompt_en: After grazing, a goat rests and chews food that has returned to its mouth. What is this returned food called?
openers.prompt_hi: Charne ke baad bakri aaraam karte hue munh mein wapas aaya khaana chabaati hai. Is wapas aaye khaane ko kya kehte hain?
hints: Is the goat chewing freshly picked grass?
Ruminants bring partly digested food back for more chewing.
This returned, partly digested food is called ____.
Cud: it returns to the mouth for further chewing.

harder.prompt_en: At a pond, a frog catches an insect with its tongue; a dragonfly breaks an insect into pieces with its jaws. Which one swallows its food whole: the frog or the dragonfly?
harder.prompt_hi: Talaab par mendhak jeebh se keeda pakadta hai; dragonfly apne jabdon se keede ke tukde karti hai. Khaana poora kaun nigalta hai: mendhak ya dragonfly?
harder.answer: Frog
hints: Which animal is described as breaking food into pieces?
Swallowing whole means not breaking the prey up first.
The animal that does not break it into pieces is ____.
Frog: unlike the dragonfly, it swallows the insect whole.

harder.prompt_en: During a school farm visit, a buffalo swallows grass quickly, then chews while resting. Why does the grass return to its mouth?
harder.prompt_hi: School farm visit mein bhains jaldi ghaas nigalti hai, phir aaraam karte hue chabaati hai. Ghaas uske munh mein wapas kyun aati hai?
harder.answer: To chew the partly digested grass more thoroughly
acceptable: dobara achchhi tarah chabaane ke liye
hints: Did the buffalo chew the grass thoroughly while grazing?
Think about what more chewing does to coarse grass.
The grass returns so the buffalo can ____.
It returns for further chewing after being swallowed quickly.

verified.solverAnswer: To chew it properly as cud
verified.note: Both explain re-chewing cud for thorough digestion

harder.prompt_en: A microscope video shows an amoeba extending pseudopodia around a food particle. After the particle is enclosed, where is it digested: in a food vacuole or in the pseudopodia?
harder.prompt_hi: Microscope video mein amoeba food particle ke ird-gird pseudopodia badhaata hai. Particle ghir jaane ke baad woh kahan digest hota hai: food vacuole mein ya pseudopodia mein?
harder.answer: Food vacuole
hints: What job do the pseudopodia do first?
Look for the enclosed space formed after food enters.
Digestion happens inside the ____.
Food vacuole: it holds the engulfed particle while digestion occurs.

openers.prompt_en: A cricketer takes air into her lungs, then her leg cells use oxygen to release energy from food. Which action is respiration: air entering the lungs or energy being released in leg cells?
openers.prompt_hi: Ek cricketer apne lungs mein hawa leti hai. Phir uske pair ki cells oxygen use karke food se energy nikaalti hain. Respiration kaunsi action hai: lungs mein hawa jaana ya leg cells mein energy release hona?
openers.answer: Energy being released in leg cells
acceptable: leg cells mein energy release hona
hints: Which action happens inside cells?
Breathing moves air; respiration uses food inside cells.
Respiration is the action in the ____.
Energy release in leg cells is respiration because it happens in cells.

verified.solverAnswer: Energy being released in leg cells

openers.prompt_en: During a school choir rehearsal, Meera breathes in deeply. Does her chest cavity become larger or smaller as air enters her lungs?
openers.prompt_hi: School choir rehearsal mein Meera gehri saans andar leti hai. Jab lungs mein hawa jaati hai, uski chest cavity badi hoti hai ya chhoti?
hints: What change gives the lungs room to fill?
Think about how inhaling changes space inside the chest.
As air enters, the chest cavity becomes ____.
Larger: inhaling expands the chest cavity, helping air enter.

harder.prompt_en: A runner is breathing normally, but oxygen cannot reach her muscle cells. Why would her muscles still struggle to keep running?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek runner ki breathing normal hai, lekin oxygen uski muscle cells tak nahi pahunch paati. Phir bhi uski muscles ko daudte rehne mein dikkat kyun hogi?
harder.answer: The muscle cells cannot use oxygen to release enough energy from food.
acceptable: not enough energy is released from food in muscle cells
muscle cells ko food se kaafi energy nahi milegi
hints: Is moving air into the lungs enough for working muscles?
Focus on what muscle cells need to do with food.
Without oxygen in muscle cells, food releases less ____.
Muscles struggle because their cells cannot release enough energy from food.

verified.solverAnswer: Without oxygen, less energy is released from food.
verified.note: Both state insufficient energy release without oxygen

harder.prompt_en: Two sealed jars contain equal volumes of air: one was filled with fresh outdoor air, the other with air students breathed out. Which jar has more carbon dioxide: the outdoor-air jar or the breathed-out-air jar?
harder.prompt_hi: Do sealed jars mein barabar hawa hai: ek mein fresh outdoor air, doosre mein students ki saans se nikli hawa. Kis jar mein carbon dioxide zyada hogi: outdoor-air jar ya breathed-out-air jar?
harder.answer: The breathed-out-air jar
acceptable: saans se nikli hawa wala jar
hints: Which air has already passed through the body?
Cells produce a gas that leaves when we exhale.
More carbon dioxide is in the ____ jar.
The breathed-out-air jar has more because exhalation removes carbon dioxide.

harder.prompt_en: After a school garden is watered, an earthworm moves across a wet path. If the path dries completely, why must it reach moist soil to keep breathing?
harder.prompt_hi: School garden mein paani dene ke baad ek earthworm geele raste par aa gaya. Agar rasta poori tarah sookh jaaye, toh saans lete rehne ke liye use nam mitti tak kyun pahunchna hoga?
harder.answer: An earthworm takes in oxygen through its moist skin.
acceptable: oxygen enters through its moist skin
woh nam skin se oxygen leta hai
hints: Which body surface is exposed to the path?
Think about the condition that surface needs for gas exchange.
The earthworm takes in oxygen through its moist ____.
It needs moisture because oxygen enters through its moist skin.

verified.solverAnswer: Its skin must stay moist for gas exchange.
verified.note: Both require moist skin for earthworm respiration

openers.prompt_en: A spinach plant grows new leaves in a sunny school garden. Where does it make the glucose used for growth: in its green leaves or in the soil?
openers.prompt_hi: School garden mein palak ke paudhe par dhoop mein naye patte ugte hain. Growth ke liye glucose kahan banta hai: hare patton mein ya mitti mein?
hints: Which part of the plant gets light and looks green?
Think of the part where photosynthesis happens.
The plant makes glucose in its ___.
Green leaves: photosynthesis makes glucose there.

openers.prompt_en: A science club grows mint in water under a lamp. The roots get water, and the green leaves get light. Which gas must the leaves take in to make food: carbon dioxide or oxygen?
openers.prompt_hi: Science club lamp ke neeche paani mein pudina uga raha hai. Jad ko paani aur hare patton ko light milti hai. Food banane ke liye patte kaunsi gas lete hain: carbon dioxide ya oxygen?
hints: Which gas enters leaves during photosynthesis?
Think about the gas plants use alongside water.
For food-making, leaves take in ___.
Carbon dioxide: leaves use it with water to make food.

harder.prompt_en: A sealed classroom plant chamber has water, a bright lamp and green leaves, but its carbon dioxide is removed. Which addition would let the plant make glucose again: carbon dioxide or extra oxygen?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek band classroom plant chamber mein paani, bright lamp aur hare patte hain, par carbon dioxide hata di gayi hai. Paudha phir se glucose bana sake, iske liye kya daaloge: carbon dioxide ya extra oxygen?
harder.answer: Carbon dioxide
hints: Which material needed for food-making is missing?
Light and water are present; check the gas supply.
To restart food-making, add ___.
Carbon dioxide: it is a raw material for making glucose.

harder.prompt_en: A variegated leaf has green and white patches. Both receive sunlight. After an iodine starch test, only green patches turn blue-black. Why did the white patches not make starch?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek chitkabre patte par hare aur safed dhabbe hain. Dono ko dhoop milti hai. Iodine starch test mein sirf hare dhabbe neele-kaale hote hain. Safed dhabbon mein starch kyun nahi bana?
harder.answer: The white patches lack chlorophyll needed for photosynthesis.
acceptable: No chlorophyll in the white patches
Safed dhabbon mein chlorophyll nahi hai
hints: What differs between the two patches besides their colour?
Consider the green substance needed to use light.
The white patches cannot photosynthesise because they lack ___.
They lack chlorophyll, which is needed for photosynthesis.

verified.solverAnswer: They lack chlorophyll, so no photosynthesis occurs.

harder.prompt_en: A basil plant is kept by a window all day, then in a dark room overnight. At midnight, which processes are happening in its leaves: respiration only, photosynthesis only, or both?
harder.prompt_hi: Tulsi ka paudha poora din khidki ke paas tha, phir raat bhar andhere kamre mein rakha gaya. Aadhi raat ko uske patton mein kya chal raha hoga: sirf respiration, sirf photosynthesis, ya dono?
harder.answer: Respiration only
hints: Is there light in the room at midnight?
One process needs light; the other continues at night.
At midnight, the leaves carry out ___.
Respiration only: photosynthesis needs light, but respiration continues at night.

openers.prompt_en: In a microscope image of a spinach leaf, a tiny opening has one curved cell on each side. What are these two cells called?
openers.prompt_hi: Spinach ke patte ki microscope image mein ek chhote se opening ke dono taraf ek-ek mudi hui cell hai. In do cells ko kya kehte hain?
hints: What helps the opening change its size?
Name the cells that control a stoma.
The cells beside the opening are called ___ cells.
Guard cells; they control whether the tiny opening is open or closed.

openers.prompt_en: A coriander plant on a balcony is making food in bright sunlight. Which gas must enter its leaves through stomata for this process: oxygen or carbon dioxide?
openers.prompt_hi: Balcony mein coriander ka paudha tez dhoop mein food bana raha hai. Is process ke liye stomata se patton mein kaunsi gas enter karegi: oxygen ya carbon dioxide?
hints: Which process lets a plant make food in sunlight?
Think of the gas that process uses as a raw material.
To make food, the leaf takes in ___.
Carbon dioxide; the leaf uses it to make food in sunlight.

harder.prompt_en: During a hot afternoon, the two guard cells around a stoma lose water and become less swollen. Will that stoma open wider or become narrower?
harder.prompt_hi: Garam dopahar mein ek stoma ke aas-paas ki do guard cells paani kho kar kam phooli hui ho jaati hain. Kya stoma aur khulega ya sankra ho jayega?
harder.answer: Become narrower
hints: What changes when these cells lose water?
Their swelling helps set the size of the opening.
Less swelling makes the opening ___.
Narrower; less-swollen guard cells no longer hold it as wide open.

harder.prompt_en: A school greenhouse is dark after sunset, so its plants cannot make food using light. Why can its leaves still take in oxygen through stomata?
harder.prompt_hi: Sunset ke baad school greenhouse mein andhera hai, isliye paudhe light se food nahi bana sakte. Phir bhi unke patte stomata se oxygen kyun le sakte hain?
harder.answer: Plants continue to respire in darkness and need oxygen for respiration.
acceptable: saans lene ke liye oxygen chahiye
paudhe raat ko bhi respiration karte hain
hints: Does every life process stop when sunlight disappears?
Making food needs light, but another process continues.
The leaves need oxygen for ___.
Respiration; plants keep using oxygen to release energy after sunset.

verified.solverAnswer: Respiration continues without light and needs oxygen.
verified.note: Both explain respiration needs oxygen.

harder.prompt_en: A school covers the leaves of one plant with a thin waterproof coating that blocks its stomata. Both plants get equal water. Which plant will lose less water vapour through its leaves: coated or uncoated?
harder.prompt_hi: School ek paudhe ke patton par patli waterproof coating lagata hai jo stomata block karti hai. Dono paudhon ko barabar paani milta hai. Patton se kam water vapour kaunsa paudha khoyega: coated ya uncoated?
harder.answer: Coated plant
hints: Where does water vapour usually leave a leaf?
Blocking those openings changes the route for water loss.
Less vapour escapes from the ___ plant.
Coated plant; blocked stomata reduce water-vapour loss through the leaves.

openers.prompt_en: A school gardener adds dissolved mineral fertiliser to the soil around a tomato plant. Which tissue carries the absorbed minerals from the roots up the stem: xylem or phloem?
openers.prompt_hi: School gardener tomato plant ke aas-paas ki mitti mein ghula hua mineral fertiliser daalta hai. Roots se absorb hue minerals ko stem mein upar kaunsa tissue le jaata hai: xylem ya phloem?
hints: What enters the plant through its roots?
Think of the tissue that carries water with dissolved minerals.
Roots → ___ → stem
Xylem carries absorbed water and minerals upward.

openers.prompt_en: A mango tree makes food in its leaves. Which tissue carries some of that food to a growing mango: xylem or phloem?
openers.prompt_hi: Mango tree apni leaves mein food banata hai. Us food ka kuch hissa badhte hue aam tak kaunsa tissue le jaata hai: xylem ya phloem?
hints: Where is the food made?
Food and water travel in different tissues.
Leaves → ___ → growing mango
Phloem carries food made in leaves to the fruit.

harder.prompt_en: A bean plant absorbs water containing dissolved minerals. A narrow ring of phloem is removed from its stem, but the xylem remains intact. Can the minerals still reach its upper leaves: yes or no?
harder.prompt_hi: Bean plant dissolved minerals wala paani absorb karta hai. Uske stem se phloem ki ek patli ring hata di jaati hai, par xylem salamat rehta hai. Kya minerals ab bhi upar ki leaves tak pahunch sakte hain: haan ya nahin?
harder.answer: Yes
hints: Which tissue was left intact?
Trace the route taken by water and dissolved minerals.
Minerals travel upward through ___, which remains intact.
Yes; intact xylem can still carry minerals upward.

harder.prompt_en: A plant’s leaves make sugar, while its underground roots cannot make their own food. To deliver sugar from leaves to roots, should the plant use xylem or phloem?
harder.prompt_hi: Plant ki leaves sugar banati hain, lekin zameen ke neeche ki roots apna food nahin bana sakti. Leaves se roots tak sugar pahunchane ke liye plant xylem use karega ya phloem?
harder.answer: Phloem
hints: Where must the sugar go?
Choose the tissue that transports food, not absorbed water.
Leaves → ___ → roots
Phloem carries leaf-made sugar to roots.

harder.prompt_en: Two identical potted plants have equally moist soil. One is under a fan; the other is in still air. If moving air increases transpiration, which plant will have a stronger upward pull of water: the fan plant or the still-air plant?
harder.prompt_hi: Do ek jaise potted plants ki mitti barabar geeli hai. Ek fan ke neeche hai, doosra shaant hawa mein. Agar chalti hawa transpiration badhati hai, to paani ka upward pull kismein zyada hoga: fan wala ya shaant hawa wala plant?
harder.answer: The fan plant
hints: Which plant loses water from leaves faster?
Greater transpiration creates a stronger upward pull.
More leaf-water loss → ___ upward pull.
The fan plant; increased transpiration strengthens the upward pull.

openers.prompt_en: At a school event, a glow stick shines after it is bent. Is the glowing stick luminous or non-luminous?
openers.prompt_hi: School event mein glow stick modne ke baad chamakti hai. Chamakte hue stick luminous hai ya non-luminous?
hints: Does the stick make light or only send back someone else's light?
Classify it by where the light comes from.
Because its light comes from ___, it is classified as ___.
Luminous: the glowing stick gives out its own light.

openers.prompt_en: A folder cover lets you see a bright lamp through it, but not the lamp's clear outline. Is the cover transparent, translucent or opaque?
openers.prompt_hi: Ek folder cover ke paar bright lamp dikhta hai, lekin lamp ki outline saaf nahi dikhti. Cover transparent, translucent ya opaque hai?
hints: Does any light get through the cover?
Also check whether you can see a clear outline.
Light passes through, but the image is ___; the category is ___.
Translucent: light passes through, but the outline is unclear.

harder.prompt_en: A cyclist sees a road stud shine only when her headlamp points at it. A nearby LED marker keeps shining when the headlamp is turned away. Which is luminous: the road stud or the LED marker?
harder.prompt_hi: Cyclist ko road stud sirf headlamp ki roshni padne par chamakta dikhta hai. Paas ka LED marker headlamp hatane par bhi chamakta hai. Luminous kaun hai: road stud ya LED marker?
harder.answer: LED marker
hints: Which one keeps shining without the cyclist's headlamp?
Look for the object that gives out its own light.
The luminous object is ___ because it does not need the headlamp.
LED marker: it gives out light; the road stud reflects headlamp light.

harder.prompt_en: At a science fair, one screen passes light but hides the shape of a torch behind it. A second screen blocks the light completely. What are the two screens, in order: translucent then opaque, or transparent then translucent?
harder.prompt_hi: Science fair mein pehli screen torch ki roshni guzarne deti hai, par uski shape chhupa deti hai. Doosri screen roshni bilkul rok deti hai. Kram mein screens kaunsi hain: translucent phir opaque, ya transparent phir translucent?
harder.answer: Translucent then opaque
hints: What happens to the light at each screen?
Use both clues: light passing through and a visible shape.
The first screen is ___; the second is ___.
Translucent then opaque: the first passes some light; the second blocks it.

harder.prompt_en: A cricket ball lies under a desk in a dark room. Riya switches on a lamp and can see the ball. Why can she see it now? Answer with the path light takes.
harder.prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein cricket ball desk ke neeche padi hai. Riya lamp jalati hai aur ball dekh pati hai. Ab ball kyun dikhti hai? Roshni ka raasta batao.
harder.answer: Light from the lamp reflects off the ball into Riya's eyes.
acceptable: lamp ki roshni ball se takrakar Riya ki aankhon mein aati hai
Light from the lamp bounces off the ball into her eyes.
hints: What must reach Riya's eyes for her to see the ball?
Trace the light from its source to the object and then onward.
The path is lamp → ___ → Riya's eyes.
Lamp → ball → eyes: light reflects off the ball into Riya's eyes.

verified.solverAnswer: Light from the lamp reflects off the ball into her eyes.
verified.note: Identical reflection path answers.

openers.prompt_en: A phone flashlight shines through a straight straw onto a desk. You put an opaque coin directly between the straw and the desk. Why does a dark patch appear on the desk?
openers.prompt_hi: Phone ki flashlight seedhi straw se hokar desk par padti hai. Tum straw aur desk ke beech ek apaaradarshi sikka rakhte ho. Desk par kaala hissa kyun dikhta hai?
openers.answer: The coin blocks the straight-travelling light from reaching that part of the desk.
acceptable: The coin blocks the light reaching that part of the desk
Sikka seedhi chalti roshni ko desk tak pahunchne se rokta hai
hints: Which part of the desk can the coin hide from the flashlight?
Think about the path light takes after leaving the straw.
The coin stops light from reaching ___ of the desk.
The coin blocks straight-travelling light, leaving that part of the desk dark.

verified.solverAnswer: The coin blocks light, and light travels in straight lines.
verified.note: Solver adds light path but omits blocking.

openers.prompt_en: At a school exhibition, a cardboard cut-out is held between a fixed bulb and a fixed screen. If the cut-out moves closer to the bulb, does its shadow on the screen get bigger or smaller?
openers.prompt_hi: School exhibition mein cardboard cut-out ek fixed bulb aur fixed screen ke beech hai. Cut-out ko bulb ke paas le jaane par screen par uski parchhaai badi hogi ya chhoti?
hints: Imagine rays leaving the bulb and passing the cut-out’s edges.
The rays spread out as they travel towards the screen.
Moving the cut-out towards the bulb makes the blocked region ___.
Bigger: near the bulb, the cut-out blocks a wider spread of rays.

harder.prompt_en: During a science fair, a torch shines towards a screen through two cardboard sheets with small holes. The holes are not aligned, so no bright spot appears. Why can’t the light reach the screen through both holes?
harder.prompt_hi: Science fair mein torch ki roshni do cardboard sheets ke chhote chhedon se screen ki taraf jaati hai. Chhed ek seedh mein nahin hain, isliye bright spot nahin banta. Roshni dono chhedon se hokar screen tak kyun nahin pahunchti?
harder.answer: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend to pass through both unaligned holes.
acceptable: Light travels straight and cannot pass through both holes
Roshni seedhi chalti hai; mudkar dono chhedon se nahin ja sakti
hints: What path would connect the torch to both holes?
Recall how light travels through air.
To pass through both holes, the path would need to ___.
Light travels straight; it cannot turn to pass through unaligned holes.

verified.solverAnswer: Light travels in straight lines, so it cannot bend through misaligned holes.
verified.note: Both cite straight-line travel preventing bend.

harder.prompt_en: A rectangular tablet is held upright between a torch and a wall. First it faces the torch; then it is turned edge-on without changing its distance from the torch. Will its shadow on the wall become wider or narrower?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek rectangular tablet torch aur deewar ke beech seedha pakda hai. Pehle uska saamna torch ki taraf hai; phir bina doori badle use kinare ki taraf ghumaate hain. Deewar par parchhaai chaudi hogi ya patli?
harder.answer: Narrower
hints: Compare what the torch sees in each position.
Shadow shape depends on the object’s orientation to the light.
Turned edge-on, the tablet blocks a ___ width of light.
Narrower: its edge blocks less width than its broad face.

harder.prompt_en: At a metro station, Meera sees her face with details in a polished steel panel and a dark outline of her head on the floor. Which one is a reflection, and which is a shadow?
harder.prompt_hi: Metro station par Meera ko polished steel panel mein apna chehra details ke saath dikhta hai, aur farsh par sirf sir ki kaali outline dikhti hai. Inmein reflection kaunsa hai aur shadow kaunsi?
harder.answer: The face in the steel panel is a reflection; the dark outline on the floor is a shadow.
acceptable: Panel mein reflection, farsh par shadow
Steel mein pratibimb, farsh par parchhaai
hints: Which sight shows facial details?
Compare bounced light with an area where light is blocked.
The detailed face is ___; the dark outline is ___.
The panel shows a reflection; blocked light makes the floor shadow.

verified.solverAnswer: The polished steel panel shows a reflection, and the floor shows a shadow.
verified.note: Both identify reflection vs shadow correctly.

openers.prompt_en: Sunlight falls on a glossy phone screen and a matte phone case. Which surface is more likely to show a clear reflection of a window: the screen or the case?
openers.prompt_hi: Dhoop ek glossy phone screen aur matte phone case par padti hai. Khidki ka saaf reflection kismein dikhne ki zyada sambhavna hai: screen ya case?
hints: Which surface looks smoother?
A smooth surface sends reflected light in an orderly way.
The clearer reflection will appear on the ___ surface.
The screen: its smooth surface reflects light more regularly.

openers.prompt_en: A trophy is placed 1.5 m in front of a plane mirror at a school exhibition. How far behind the mirror does its image appear?
openers.prompt_hi: School exhibition mein ek trophy plane mirror se 1.5 m aage rakhi hai. Uski image mirror ke peeche kitni door dikhegi?
hints: Where does the image appear relative to the mirror?
Compare its distance with the trophy’s distance in front.
Distance behind the mirror = ___ in front.
1.5 m: a plane-mirror image appears equally far behind.

harder.prompt_en: At a school event, a smooth metal tray shows a clear reflection of ceiling lights, but a scratched tray does not. Why, though both reflect light?
harder.prompt_hi: School event mein smooth metal tray par ceiling lights ka saaf reflection dikhta hai, lekin scratched tray par nahi. Dono light reflect karte hain, phir bhi aisa kyun?
harder.answer: The scratches scatter reflected light in different directions, so no clear image forms.
acceptable: reflected light goes in different directions
hints: What changed on the tray’s surface?
Think about whether reflected rays stay orderly.
Scratches make reflected light go in ___ directions.
Scratches scatter light in different directions, preventing a clear image.

verified.solverAnswer: The smooth tray gives regular reflection; the scratched tray gives irregular reflection.
verified.note: Solver names reflection types, key explains scattering.

harder.prompt_en: Meera stands 2 m from a plane mirror, then steps 0.5 m towards it. After the step, how far is Meera from her image?
harder.prompt_hi: Meera plane mirror se 2 m door khadi hai, phir 0.5 m uski taraf badhti hai. Ab Meera aur uski image ke beech kitni doori hai?
harder.answer: 3 m
hints: How far is Meera from the mirror after stepping?
The image is equally far behind the mirror.
Meera-to-image distance = new distance in front + ___ behind.
3 m: she is 1.5 m in front and her image 1.5 m behind.

harder.prompt_en: In a science demo, a laser ray strikes a plane mirror at 25° to its surface. What angle does the reflected ray make with the normal, the line perpendicular to the mirror?
harder.prompt_hi: Science demo mein laser ray plane mirror ki surface se 25° ka angle banakar takrati hai. Reflected ray normal, yaani mirror par seedhi khadi line, se kitna angle banayegi?
hints: Is the given angle measured from the surface or the normal?
The surface and normal make a right angle; reflected and incident angles match.
Angle to normal = 90° − ___; reflection keeps that angle.
65°: the incident angle to the normal is 90° − 25°.

openers.prompt_en: A pinhole camera faces a school poster with a red stripe at the top and a blue stripe at the bottom. Which stripe appears at the top of the image on its screen: red or blue?
openers.prompt_hi: Pinhole camera ke saamne school poster hai: upar red stripe aur neeche blue stripe. Camera ki screen par image ke upar kaunsi stripe dikhegi: red ya blue?
hints: Where does light from the poster’s lower edge land?
Trace its path straight through the tiny hole.
The lower stripe appears at the ___ of the screen.
Blue: its light crosses the hole and reaches the screen’s top.

openers.prompt_en: At a crowded school match, Riya makes a periscope with two plane mirrors. Which arrangement lets her see over the crowd: mirrors parallel at 45° to the tube, or mirrors flat across the tube?
openers.prompt_hi: Crowded school match mein Riya do plane mirrors se periscope banati hai. Crowd ke upar dekhne ke liye kaunsa arrangement sahi hai: mirrors tube se 45° par parallel, ya tube ke across flat?
openers.answer: Mirrors parallel at 45° to the tube
hints: Which arrangement sends light down, then towards her eye?
Each mirror must redirect the light along the tube’s path.
Choose mirrors placed ___ to the tube.
Parallel at 45°: the two reflections carry light down and out.

verified.solverAnswer: mirrors parallel at 45° to the tube

harder.prompt_en: A pinhole camera shows an image of a lit stage sign. Without moving the sign or pinhole, Aarav moves the screen farther from the hole. Will the image become larger or smaller?
harder.prompt_hi: Pinhole camera mein lit stage sign ki image dikh rahi hai. Sign aur pinhole ko bina hilaaye Aarav screen ko hole se door karta hai. Image badi hogi ya chhoti?
harder.answer: Larger
hints: What happens to the gap between spreading light rays?
After crossing the hole, rays keep travelling straight apart.
Farther from the hole, their separation is ___.
Larger: the rays spread farther apart before reaching the screen.

harder.prompt_en: A metro-platform periscope has a top and a bottom mirror. Why would keeping only the top mirror fail to let you see over a tall barrier? Give the missing step in the light’s path.
harder.prompt_hi: Metro platform ke periscope mein upar aur neeche ek-ek mirror hai. Sirf upar wala mirror rakhne se tall barrier ke paar kyun nahi dekh paoge? Light ke path mein missing step batao.
harder.answer: The bottom mirror must reflect the light from down the tube into your eye.
acceptable: bottom mirror sends light to the eye
neeche wala mirror light aankh tak reflect karta hai
hints: After the top mirror, where is the light travelling?
Your eye is beside the tube’s lower opening.
A second reflection turns the light towards ___.
The bottom mirror reflects light into your eye; without it, light travels down.

verified.solverAnswer: The bottom mirror is needed to reflect light from the top mirror into the eye.
verified.note: Both specify bottom mirror's role in path.

harder.prompt_en: Meera puts a few coloured glass pieces inside a kaleidoscope made with three mirror strips. Why does she see many repeating shapes rather than just the few pieces she put in?
harder.prompt_hi: Meera teen mirror strips wale kaleidoscope mein kuch coloured glass pieces daalti hai. Use sirf wahi kuch pieces nahi, balki bahut saari repeating shapes kyun dikhti hain?
harder.answer: Light reflects repeatedly between the mirrors, producing multiple images of the pieces.
acceptable: mirrors mein baar-baar reflection se kai images banti hain
hints: Can an image in one mirror appear in another?
Follow light as it bounces between the mirror strips.
Repeated reflections create many ___ of each piece.
Multiple images: light reflects repeatedly between the mirrors.

verified.solverAnswer: Multiple reflections between the mirrors create repeated symmetrical patterns.
verified.note: Both describe multiple reflections creating images.

openers.prompt_en: A satellite image shows Bengaluru on the dark side of Earth. Which movement will bring Bengaluru into sunlight: Earth's rotation on its axis or Earth's revolution around the Sun?
openers.prompt_hi: Satellite image mein Bengaluru Earth ke andhere waale hisse par hai. Bengaluru ko dhoop mein kaunsi movement laayegi: Earth ka apni axis par ghoomna ya Sun ke chaaron taraf ghoomna?
hints: Which movement changes the side of Earth a city faces?
Think about how a place moves between darkness and sunlight.
Bengaluru enters sunlight as Earth _____ on its axis.
Rotation: it carries Bengaluru from the dark side into sunlight.

openers.prompt_en: Two students check sunrise from Kolkata and Jaipur on the same morning. Which city sees sunrise earlier: Kolkata or Jaipur?
openers.prompt_hi: Do students ek hi subah Kolkata aur Jaipur se sunrise check karte hain. Sunrise pehle kahaan dikhega: Kolkata ya Jaipur?
hints: Which city lies farther east?
Earth's turning brings eastern places into sunlight first.
The farther-east city, _____, sees sunrise earlier.
Kolkata: it lies east of Jaipur and turns into sunlight first.

harder.prompt_en: At noon, a school ground in Pune faces the Sun. Earth makes one rotation in about 24 hours. About 12 hours later, will that ground face towards or away from the Sun?
harder.prompt_hi: Dopahar ko Pune ka school ground Sun ki taraf hai. Earth lagbhag 24 ghante mein ek baar ghoomti hai. Kareeb 12 ghante baad ground Sun ki taraf hoga ya usse door?
harder.answer: Away from the Sun
hints: What fraction of a full turn happens in that time?
Half a rotation changes which side faces the Sun.
After half a turn, the ground faces _____ the Sun.
Away from the Sun: half a rotation turns the ground to Earth's dark side.

harder.prompt_en: During a night cricket match, a star seems to shift towards the west above the stadium. Why does it appear to move that way? Answer using Earth's direction of rotation.
harder.prompt_hi: Night cricket match ke dauraan stadium ke upar ek taara pashchim ki taraf khisakta dikhta hai. Aisa kyun dikhta hai? Earth ke ghoomne ki disha se jawaab do.
harder.answer: Earth rotates from west to east, so the star appears to move east to west.
acceptable: Earth turns east, making the star seem to move west
Earth poorab ki taraf ghoomti hai, isliye taara pashchim jaata dikhta hai
hints: Could the observer's movement affect what seems to move?
The sky appears to shift opposite Earth's direction of rotation.
Earth rotates from _____ to _____, so the star seems to shift oppositely.
Earth rotates west to east, making the star appear to move towards the west.

verified.solverAnswer: Earth rotates from west to east, so stars appear to move westward.
verified.note: Identical meaning

harder.prompt_en: Earth takes about 365¼ days to complete one revolution around the Sun. A calendar usually counts 365 days per year. Why is an extra day added about every four years?
harder.prompt_hi: Earth ko Sun ka ek chakkar lagaane mein lagbhag 365¼ din lagte hain. Calendar aam taur par saal mein 365 din ginta hai. Kareeb har chaar saal baad ek extra din kyun jodte hain?
harder.answer: The extra quarter-day each year adds up to one day in four years.
acceptable: Har saal ka chauthai din chaar saal mein ek din ban jaata hai
hints: What part of a day does the calendar leave out yearly?
The leftover time accumulates rather than disappearing.
Over four years, the leftover parts total _____ day.
Four quarter-days total one day, so the calendar adds it.

verified.solverAnswer: To compensate for the extra ¼ day each year.
verified.note: Equivalent explanations

openers.prompt_en: A school globe is carried around a lamp to model Earth's orbit. To keep the model accurate, should its tilted axis keep pointing towards the same wall or turn to face the lamp?
openers.prompt_hi: Earth ki orbit dikhane ke liye school globe ko lamp ke around le jaate hain. Model sahi rakhne ke liye uski tilted axis ek hi wall ki taraf rahe ya ghoomkar lamp ki taraf ho?
openers.answer: Keep pointing towards the same wall
hints: As the globe moves, what happens to its axis?
Think about whether Earth's axis turns to follow the Sun.
Keep the axis pointing towards the same ___.
Same wall: Earth's axis keeps pointing in one direction in space.

openers.prompt_en: In a model of Earth's orbit, Kerala is in the hemisphere tilted towards the Sun. At noon there, will sunlight fall more directly or more slantingly than when that hemisphere tilts away?
openers.prompt_hi: Earth ki orbit ke model mein Kerala wala hemisphere Sun ki taraf tilted hai. Wahan dopahar ki sunlight zyada seedhi padegi ya zyada tirchhi, us samay ke muqaable jab hemisphere Sun se door tilted ho?
hints: Which way is Kerala's hemisphere tilted?
Tilt changes the angle at which sunlight reaches a place.
When tilted towards the Sun, the rays are more ___.
More directly: the hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun.

harder.prompt_en: A planetarium model shows Earth on opposite sides of its orbit in June and December. One student keeps its tilted axis parallel in both positions; another turns the axis to face the Sun each time. Whose model is accurate: first or second?
harder.prompt_hi: Planetarium model mein Earth June aur December mein orbit ki opposite sides par hai. Ek student axis ko dono jagah parallel rakhta hai; doosra har baar Sun ki taraf ghumata hai. Kiska model sahi hai: pehle ka ya doosre ka?
harder.answer: First
acceptable: the student keeping the axes parallel
hints: Does Earth's axis follow the Sun around its orbit?
Compare the axis directions in the two positions.
The accurate model is the ___ student's.
First: Earth's axis stays pointed in nearly the same direction.

harder.prompt_en: A weather report says Jaipur receives more hours of daylight in June than in December. Why can this help make June warmer, even before considering the angle of sunlight?
harder.prompt_hi: Weather report kehta hai ki Jaipur mein June mein December se zyada ghante daylight rehti hai. Sunlight ka angle soche bina bhi, isse June zyada garam kyun ho sakta hai?
harder.answer: The ground receives sunlight for more hours each day
acceptable: zameen ko zyada der dhoop milti hai
hints: For how long does sunlight reach Jaipur each day?
Consider the total time available for warming.
More daylight means the ground receives sunlight for ___ hours.
More hours of sunlight give the ground more time to warm.

verified.solverAnswer: Longer daylight hours mean more solar energy absorbed.
verified.note: Similar core idea

harder.prompt_en: In July, a match in England has long, warm evenings, while a match in South Africa has short, cool days. Why does this difference rule out Earth's distance from the Sun as the main cause of seasons?
harder.prompt_hi: July mein England ke match mein shaamein lambi aur garam hain, jabki South Africa ke match mein din chhote aur thande hain. Yeh fark Earth ki Sun se doori ko seasons ki main wajah kyun nahi maanta?
harder.answer: Both hemispheres are nearly the same distance from the Sun, yet have opposite seasons because of Earth's tilt
acceptable: same distance but opposite seasons due to tilt
doori lagbhag ek jaisi hai, par tilt se seasons ulte hain
hints: Are these places on separate planets?
Compare their distance from the Sun with their seasons.
Their Sun-distance is nearly ___, but their seasons differ.
Both share nearly the same Sun-distance; Earth's tilt gives them opposite seasons.

verified.solverAnswer: Opposing seasons in two hemispheres at equal distance from Sun disproves distance cause.
verified.note: Same reasoning

openers.prompt_en: During a solar eclipse, a school in Jaipur sees the Sun partly covered, but a school in Kochi does not. Which school is in the Moon’s shadow: Jaipur or Kochi?
openers.prompt_hi: Solar eclipse ke waqt Jaipur ke school ko Sooraj ka kuch hissa dhaka dikhta hai, lekin Kochi ke school ko nahi. Moon ki shadow mein kaunsa school hai: Jaipur ya Kochi?
hints: At which school does the Sun appear partly covered?
The covering is visible where the Moon blocks sunlight.
The school in the Moon’s shadow is ___.
Jaipur: its view of the Sun is partly blocked by the Moon.

openers.prompt_en: At a night-time skywatch, the Moon moves into Earth’s shadow. Which object is between the Sun and the Moon: Earth or Mars?
openers.prompt_hi: Raat ke skywatch mein Moon, Earth ki shadow mein aa jaata hai. Sun aur Moon ke beech kaunsa object hai: Earth ya Mars?
hints: Whose shadow is reaching the Moon?
A shadow forms behind the object blocking sunlight.
Sun → ___ → Moon.
Earth: it blocks sunlight and casts its shadow on the Moon.

harder.prompt_en: During a solar eclipse, students in Surat see the Sun completely covered; students in Vadodara see only part covered. Which city lies in the Moon’s darkest shadow: Surat or Vadodara?
harder.prompt_hi: Solar eclipse ke waqt Surat ke students ko Sooraj poora dhaka dikhta hai; Vadodara mein sirf kuch hissa dhakta hai. Moon ki sabse gehri shadow mein kaunsa shehar hai: Surat ya Vadodara?
harder.answer: Surat
hints: Which city sees the Sun completely covered?
The darkest shadow blocks the whole visible Sun.
Complete covering points to ___ being in the darkest shadow.
Surat: the Moon blocks the whole Sun from there.

harder.prompt_en: On one full-moon night, Earth’s shadow darkens the Moon. On another, no eclipse occurs. Why can both nights have a full Moon?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek purnima ki raat Earth ki shadow Moon ko dark kar deti hai. Doosri purnima par eclipse nahi hota. Dono raat full Moon kaise ho sakta hai?
harder.answer: The Moon’s orbit is tilted, so a full Moon usually passes above or below Earth’s shadow.
acceptable: The Moon's tilted orbit usually takes it past Earth's shadow
Moon ki orbit tilted hai, isliye woh aksar Earth ki shadow se bachkar nikalta hai
hints: Must a full Moon always enter Earth’s shadow?
Think about the tilt of the Moon’s path.
Usually, the Moon passes ___ Earth’s shadow.
Its orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below Earth’s shadow.

verified.solverAnswer: Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below Earth's shadow.

harder.prompt_en: Your school has no certified eclipse glasses. For a solar eclipse, should your group watch the Sun through sunglasses or view its image projected through a small hole onto paper?
harder.prompt_hi: School mein certified eclipse glasses nahi hain. Solar eclipse ke liye group sunglasses se Sun dekhe ya chhote hole se paper par bani uski image dekhe?
harder.answer: View its image projected through a small hole onto paper.
acceptable: project the Sun’s image onto paper
chhote hole se paper par bani image dekhein
hints: Which option avoids looking towards the Sun?
Ordinary sunglasses do not make direct viewing safe.
Choose the method that shows an ___ rather than the Sun itself.
View the projected image: you can observe it without looking at the Sun.

verified.solverAnswer: view its image projected through a small hole onto paper
